content.value_statement: Canton and DAML work often requires tracing versions across several repositories. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code explain repository roles, build paths, and compatibility risks.
actual_capabilities: Explains roles of DAML SDK, Canton runtime, and Splice repositories.
Maps selected Splice, Canton, DAML SDK, protocol, and LF versions.
Identifies key files for LF versions, package targets, and build settings.
Summarizes community and enterprise Canton differences from the guide.
Provides build and troubleshooting guidance for LF target mismatches.
limitations: Does not execute builds or verify current upstream repository state.
Version notes may become outdated as Canton Network projects release updates.
Focuses on documented open-source paths, not private enterprise source code.
Does not replace official release notes or security advisories.

use_cases.title: Trace Version Compatibility
use_cases.description: Understand how Splice, Canton, DAML SDK, protocol, and LF versions relate before changing package targets.

use_cases.title: Plan Open-Source Builds
use_cases.description: Find repository areas and build steps involved in community Canton and Splice application builds.

use_cases.title: Debug Package ID Changes
use_cases.description: Investigate package ID mismatches caused by LF targets, SDK versions, dependencies, or rebuild choices.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Repository Roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how DAML SDK, Canton, and Splice relate in the Canton Network ecosystem. Keep it concise.

prompt_templates.title: Find Relevant Files
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to inspect LF version settings in Canton Network repositories. List the key files and what each file controls.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an LF Target Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an open-source Splice update from LF 2.1 to LF 2.2. Include build files, package targets, and compatibility checks.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Package Mismatch
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a Canton package ID mismatch after changing SDK versions. Use the Canton Network repository guidance to identify likely causes and checks.

output_examples.input: Explain why changing the LF target affects package IDs.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that package IDs include source content, LF version, SDK libraries, and dependency package IDs. Changing LF targets changes hashes and can break upgrade validation.

output_examples.input: Where should I look before updating Splice to a newer DAML SDK?
output_examples.output: Review version configuration, compiler sources, package target settings, and DAML package manifests. Confirm all packages use the same LF target before rebuilding.

output_examples.input: Compare community and enterprise Canton from this guide.
output_examples.output: It summarizes differences in application entry points, transaction processing, pruning, database support, and high availability domain support.

best_practices: Cross-check version guidance with official release pages before changing builds.
Keep LF target, SDK version, and dependency package IDs consistent.
Treat build commands as examples and review them before running.
anti_patterns: Mixing LF targets across related DAML packages.
Assuming community packages are interchangeable with enterprise packages.
Updating SDK versions without rebuilding and comparing package IDs.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides repository guidance and example commands. The user or agent must choose whether to run them.

faq.question: Which repositories does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers DAML SDK, Canton, and decentralized-canton-sync, also known as Splice.

faq.question: Can it verify the latest releases?
faq.answer: No. It lists external release pages, but current release checks require browsing or repository inspection.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What problems does it help debug?
faq.answer: It helps debug LF target issues, package ID mismatches, and version compatibility across Canton Network components.

faq.question: Does it include enterprise source code?
faq.answer: No. It describes community and enterprise differences using the provided guide, not private source code.
